name: Claude-Louis Berthollet
summary: Eminent French chemist of the 18th and early 19th centuries known for work on chemical affinities, nomenclature, and dyeing.

name: Louis Berthollet
summary: Father of Claude-Louis Berthollet, a notary and castellan.

name: Philiberte Donier
summary: Mother of Claude-Louis Berthollet.

name: Marguerite-Marie Baur
summary: Wife of Claude-Louis Berthollet.

name: Amédée-Barthélemy Berthollet
summary: Son of Claude-Louis Berthollet, collaborated on dyeing research.

name: Talloire
summary: Village in Upper Savoy where Berthollet was born.

name: Annecy
summary: Town where Berthollet first studied at a college.

name: Chambery
summary: Town where Berthollet attended college.

name: University of Turin
summary: University where Berthollet studied medicine and graduated in 1770.

name: Paris
summary: City where Berthollet continued education and worked.

name: Gobelins Manufactory
summary: Manufactory in Paris where Berthollet was administrator and dyeing director.

name: The Mint
summary: Institution where Berthollet was appointed Commissioner in 1792.

name: Commission of Agriculture and the Arts
summary: Commission of which Berthollet was named member in 1794.

name: Normal School
summary: School in Paris where Berthollet was Professor of Chemistry.

name: Napoleon Bonaparte
summary: French leader and friend of Berthollet who took him on the Egyptian campaign.

name: Gaspard Monge
summary: Mathematician and friend of Berthollet who accompanied Napoleon to Egypt.

name: L'Institut d'Égypte
summary: Institute formed in Cairo during Napoleon's campaign where Berthollet was a member.

name: French Senate
summary: Legislative body where Berthollet became a senator in 1799.

name: Académie des Sciences, Belles-Lettres et Arts de Savoie
aliases: Academy of Sciences, Belles-Lettres and Arts of Savoy
summary: Academy that elected Berthollet a member in 1820.

name: Society of Arcueil
summary: Scientific society co-founded by Berthollet and Laplace.

name: Pierre-Simon Laplace
summary: Mathematician and co-founder of the Society of Arcueil with Berthollet.

name: L'Académie Royale Des Sciences
summary: Paris academy that elected Berthollet a member in 1780.

name: La Société Hollandaise Des Sciences à Haarlem
aliases: The Dutch Society of Science in Haarlem
summary: Dutch society that elected Berthollet a foreign member in 1786.

name: L'Académie Royale Des Sciences De Turin
aliases: The Royal Academy of Sciences of Turin
summary: Turin academy that elected Berthollet a national member in 1787.

name: The Royal Society of London
summary: London society that made Berthollet a Fellow in 1789.

name: The Literary and Philosophical Society of Manchester
summary: Manchester society that elected Berthollet an honorary member in 1790.

name: Essai De Statique Chimique
summary: Two-volume book by Berthollet published in 1803 defining chemical equilibrium.

name: Méthode De Nomenclature Chimique
summary: Book jointly written by Berthollet and others in 1787.

name: Éléments De L'Art De La Teinture
summary: Book on dyeing revised by Berthollet and his son in 1804.

name: Potassium Chlorate
summary: Chemical compound first prepared in pure state by Berthollet in 1787.

name: Ammonia
summary: Alkaline gas whose composition was determined by Berthollet in 1785.

name: Prussic Acid
summary: Chemical whose composition was determined by Berthollet in 1787.

name: Sulphuretted Hydrogen
summary: Chemical whose composition was determined by Berthollet in 1789.

name: Bertholletia
summary: Genus of South American plants named after Berthollet in 1808.

name: 12750 Berthollet
summary: Asteroid named in Berthollet's honour discovered in 1993.

name: Monument to Berthollet
summary: Monument erected in Annecy in 1844 honoring Berthollet.

name: Arcueil
summary: Village where Berthollet lived and died.

name: Legion of Honour
summary: French order of merit awarded to Berthollet.

name: Order of the Reunion
summary: Order awarded to Berthollet in 1813.

name: Peer of France
summary: Title created for Berthollet by Louis XVIII in 1814.
